title: tools: app_push.sh --recarry skips prepr on a clean main merge; the merge train's recarry uses it
body:
The merge train's recarry merges `origin/main` into a pull request, and `app_push.sh` then ran `prepr.sh` before pushing. On the host that costs about 20 minutes a pull request and refuses falsely under load, and for a recarry it re-checks nothing new. tvofi decided this on #201 (comment 6070202495): a recarry skips the local `prepr` only when the push is a pure main merge with the body unchanged. CI's `pr-contract` and suite still run at the new head, and the train merges only on green.

`tools/pr/app_push.sh --recarry` reads HEAD once and judges that sha. It skips `prepr` only when all three of these hold. Each is read inside the script, and a check that cannot answer counts as failed:

- (a) HEAD has exactly two parents. Parent 1 is the pull request's live head, read from the open-pull-request listing the script already makes; that listing now runs before `prepr`, and it is a read through `gh` that mints nothing. Parent 2 is on the **first-parent chain** of `origin/main`, which the script fetches. An ancestor alone is not enough: main merges pull requests with merge commits, so an ancestor can be a merged branch's intermediate commit, a tree main never had (round-1 review).
  - The membership test is `rev-list --first-parent | grep -x "$p2" >/dev/null`, and `grep` reads to EOF.
  - Round 2 had `grep -qx`, which quits at main's tip. Under the script's `pipefail`, `rev-list` then died with SIGPIPE (exit 141) on any history longer than a pipe buffer, so every honest recarry was refused with a false reason (round-2 review). That is the same class #2067 fixes.
- (b) HEAD's tree is the tree `git merge-tree --write-tree <p1> <p2>` writes, and that merge is clean. So a conflict resolution, or any commit stacked on the merge, fails (b).
- (c) The body file, before the note, matches the live body byte for byte, ignoring trailing newlines only.

If any check fails, `prepr` runs exactly as it does without the flag. Either way the script prints one `app_push: RECARRY: prepr SKIPPED|RUNS: <why>` line. At push time the script refuses if HEAD is no longer the sha the verdict judged. `remerge_main.sh` passes the flag and forwards that line, and `merge_train.py` logs it on its recarry line.

**Where this departs from the brief, and why.** `remerge_main.sh` used to write a note under the Head section naming the new head before it pushed. `pr-contract` requires that note, because `checkPrBody` refuses a the Head section that does not name the head CI ran on. Checking (c) against a body that `remerge_main.sh` had already edited could never pass, so the skip would never fire. This change moves the note into `--recarry` and drops it from `remerge_main.sh`, so one place writes it. Check (c) runs on the unedited body, which the train writes from the API.

The note is written in both paths and always names the judged HEAD:
- **Skip path:** the note names main by parent 2's sha, read after the fetch, and says the merge took no resolution.
- **Prepr path:** the verdict has just found the push is not that merge, so the note makes no such claim. It says HEAD is the orchestrator's recarry, that it is not a clean merge (with the verdict's reason), and that `prepr` checked it.

The only body change that can bypass `prepr` is therefore the script's own note, which `pr-contract` re-checks on CI.

Alternatives I rejected:
- Strip the note before comparing: (c) would no longer be byte identity, and `app_push.sh` would depend on `remerge_main.sh`'s note format.
- Pass a second, pristine body copy: the two scripts would share the same format coupling.
- Let `update_pr.sh` use the mode: it also merges a code SHA, so its pushes are not pure recarries. It keeps `prepr`.

These still fall back to `prepr`:
- The claims-drop commit `remerge_main.sh` adds when `env_drift.py --drop-inherited` changes something. That commit gives HEAD one parent, so (a) fails.
- A live body with leading or trailing spaces, which the train's `.strip()` changes, so (c) fails.

The real-git self-test builds its repositories through `tests/throwaway_git.sh`. No new file, so nothing to classify. `tests/structure.py` passes with no budget touched.

## Head

`83826ad9cce54be2528cb796e6b0fbfba1385480` merges main `d0f085ffb` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`dfd5227d8cfdf534794ab3acd3271363287ba728` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/2069.md` (the orchestrator writes that row, per delivery-status-tracking.md; the stamp's --require-rows bar refuses an unrowed merge). The previous head was `ee43721f1dccf7154c50930e8fd6c90c13cb59e1`:

`ee43721f1dccf7154c50930e8fd6c90c13cb59e1` merges main `b2b6acd64` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`99d958b8e398e9b020b1766a20194e15ead0413a` merges main `c518447eb` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`d8988a473a4d1c282278ecee1c1b37ddd22754f5`. It is the round-2 head `e23a19ac` plus one commit, which changes only `tools/pr/app_push.sh`:
- The `grep -qx` becomes `grep -x ... >/dev/null`, with a comment saying why.
- The real-git fixture gains a main of 6000 first-parent commits.

`origin/main` (`bd59a4af`) is still contained in this head: `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD && echo "main contained"` printed `main contained`.

## Mutation proof

Every mutant was made in place on the committed tree, run through `bash tools/pr/app_push.sh --self-test`, and restored with `git checkout`.

**Round 3, at this head (91 checks):**
- The fix itself reverted: the verdict from `e23a19ac` (`| grep -qx`) under the new fixture fails:
  - FAIL `real git: the honest merge of origin/main into the same live head passes (a), (b) and (c) (null control)`;
  - FAIL `real git: the same merge amended with one more file refuses (b)`, which got the false `parent 2 ... is not on the freshly fetched origin/main's first-parent chain`;
  - FAIL `real git: a conflicted merge resolved by hand refuses (b)`, with the same false reason.
  - 3 of 91 failed.
- R1, first-parent membership put back to `merge-base --is-ancestor`: FAIL `real git: that side-branch parent 2 refuses (a)`, and 10 stub checks (11 failed).

**Round 2, measured at `aa2e80f1`** (90 checks). These lines are unchanged since; the only verdict line changed since then is R1's, re-run above.
- R2 the push-time pin `[ "$head" = "$RV_HEAD" ]` replaced by `true`: FAIL `naming both shas, and nothing was minted or pushed` (1 failed).
- R3 the skip-path note written on every path: FAIL `... and the note names the head without claiming no resolution` on all 7 refusal arms (7 failed).
- R4 the note's main sha read from `origin/main` again: FAIL `the PATCHed body names the new head, and main by parent 2's sha, ...` and `and nothing else in it moved: less the note, it is the live body` (2 failed).
- M1 the parent-1 check replaced by `true`: FAIL `... (parent 1 55555555 is not the live pull-request head 22222222)` (1 failed).
- M2 the 2-parent count replaced by `true`: FAIL `--recarry REFUSES the skip (rone)` and its line check (2 failed).
- M4 merge-tree's exit status ignored: FAIL `... (parent 1 and parent 2 do not merge cleanly)` and `real git: a conflicted merge resolved by hand refuses (b)` (2 failed).
- M5 tree equality replaced by `true`: FAIL `... (HEAD's tree is not the clean merge of its parents)` and `real git: the same merge amended with one more file refuses (b)` (2 failed).
- M6 the body comparison replaced by `sys.exit(0)`: FAIL `... (the body file is not the live pull-request body)`, `--recarry: a body edit goes to prepr, and prepr's refusal stands` and `and nothing was minted or pushed` (3 failed).
- M7 the `[ "$skip" = 1 ] ||` gate removed: FAIL `--recarry: a clean 2-parent merge ... pushed (prepr-fails set ...)`, `and prepr was skipped`, and 4 more (6 failed).

**Train side, from round 1** (`merge_train.py` and `remerge_main.sh` are unchanged since), run through `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`:
- T1 `remerge_main.sh` without `--recarry`: FAIL `remerge_main.sh pushes the recarry with app_push.sh --recarry and passes its RECARRY line on`.
- T2 the train's log without the path: FAIL `the recarry logs app_push's path line (prepr SKIPPED)` and `... (prepr RUNS)`.

## Null control

At this head, unmutated: `bash tools/pr/app_push.sh --self-test` prints `app_push self-test: 91 checks, 0 failed`, and `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` prints `merge_train self-test: 83 checks, 0 failed`.

The fixture's size is itself a check: `real git: main's first-parent list is over 64 KB, past any pipe buffer`, measured with `rev-list --first-parent origin/main | wc -c`.

The round-2 reviewer's repro, `/Users/timmalmstrom/hpo-seats/review-2069/evidence/attack_r2_sigpipe.sh <app_push.sh> /Users/timmalmstrom/heatpump_optimizer`, runs an honest recarry on this repository's real history:
- At `e23a19ac`: `run=1..3 ... pipefail=on rc=1 verdict=parent 2 421c77f9 is not on the freshly fetched origin/main's first-parent chain`, against its `control pipefail=off rc=0`.
- At `d8988a47`: `run=1..3 ... pipefail=on rc=0` (`HEAD d0045122 is the clean merge of the live head bd972508 and origin/main's 421c77f9 ...`), and the control is `rc=0`.

The round-1 reviewer's harness, `/Users/timmalmstrom/hpo-seats/review-2069/evidence/attack_p2_side.sh`, at this head: `RESULT attack=p2-side-branch rc=1 verdict=parent 2 595346d8 is not on the freshly fetched origin/main's first-parent chain`, and `control=honest-main-merge rc=0`. At `6b1d0c46` both were `rc=0`.

## Figures

- `bash tools/pr/app_push.sh --self-test`: 91 checks, 0 failed at this head (60 at `origin/main`).
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`: 83 checks, 0 failed.
- `python3 -I tests/throwaway_git.py --check`: 0 raw git init or clone sites refused. At `6b1d0c46` it refused 1, `tools/pr/app_push.sh:644`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py --check`: 0 refused, 0 stale allow entries.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run`.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --corpus-filter`: no policy path. The sentinel `CLAUDE.md` came back through the same filter.
- The early-exit reader scan, `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- tools/pr/app_push.sh tools/audit/seat/remerge_main.sh | grep -nE '^\+.*\|\s*(grep -q|grep -[a-zA-Z]*q|head|sed -n [0-9]+q|awk .*exit|python3 -c .*sys.exit)'`, matched only the round-2 `grep -qx` line, which this head replaces.
  - The other piped readers the diff adds read to EOF: `grep -E` and `grep -c`, `sed` substitution, `python3`'s `json.load(sys.stdin)`, and `wc -c`.

I did not run local `prepr.sh` (beyond the one `app_push` makes), the full suite, mutation or `derive_closures`: heavy scripts go to CI (tvofi).

## Red checks

- `instrument-self-tests` (job 113578428882, at `6b1d0c46`), red, and mine. Its step `python3 -I tests/throwaway_git.py --check` refused the raw `git init` and `git clone` in the round-1 real-git fixture at `tools/pr/app_push.sh:644`.
  - Fixed here: the fixture sources `tests/throwaway_git.sh` and uses `throwaway_git_init` and `throwaway_git_clone`. The same check now reports 0 refused.
  - A cheaper detector existed: that same check, which takes seconds locally. `prepr.sh` does not run it (`grep -n throwaway_git tools/pr/prepr.sh` finds only fixture setup), and only `governance.yml`'s instrument job does. So the check was unenforced before push, which is a process state.
  - The countermeasure (run it from `prepr.sh`, or from the fixer's pre-push list) is a change to `prepr` or to a role contract. It is outside this pull request, so it goes to the orchestrator as a root-cause item rather than being built here.
- `pr-contract` (job 113580007993, at `6b1d0c46`), red, and a consequence of the item above. `checkPrBody` refused the body because it did not name the `instrument-self-tests` red, and this section now names it.
- `nightly-status`, red at `6b1d0c46`, `e23a19ac` and `d8988a47`, and at any head a recarry of this pull request makes. It is not this pull request's: it reports `main`'s nightly run, not the head it is attached to, and nothing in this diff touches what that run grades.

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

- `fixer-brief: contradiction: the brief's (c) asks for byte identity with the live body, but remerge_main.sh edited the body before the push, and pr-contract's the Head section rule requires that edit. I resolved it by moving the note into --recarry; see the body.`
